variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: An episode starts in A (pick up the container), with the point on the first entry of target_containers computed from the demonstration at that same step: the entry just written in the memory answer for that step, so the point and the memory name the same container. Rules at any decision step: (1) If the scene shows the gripper raised with fingers partly closed (about 46% open), it is holding a container: choose B (put down the container). (2) If the fingers are fully open (about 100%) and put_down_count is less than the number of entries in target_containers, choose A and point at the container whose current listed position is nearest to target_containers[put_down_count + 1] (1-based: the first entry when put_down_count is 0, the second when it is 1); write the point as that container's listed position; a point within a few pixels of that position selects the same container, so a few pixels' difference between a listed position and an entry is never a reason to doubt the container choice. (3) If the fingers are fully open and put_down_count equals the number of entries, every named container has been handled; choose A and point at the last entry of target_containers again (harmless repeat). If a situation matches none of these rules (e.g. gripper state unclear), pick the rule whose gripper description is closest: partly closed fingers mean B, open fingers mean A on the next unhandled target.

fields.name: target_containers
fields.description: Ordered list of container positions [y, x], one per cube named in the goal instruction, in the order the goal names them. Write it at the first decision step (memory empty, demonstration steps shown) by this procedure, then copy it unchanged at every later step. Procedure: (1) from the first demonstration frames note each named cube's position; (2) at the first frame listing containers, the named cube's container is the one nearest that cube; the positions listed in that frame are the slots; label the named container by its slot; (3) go through EVERY container frame after the first one, in order, up to and including the last demonstration frame, and label each frame before doing anything else: either 'all at slots' or 'slots P and Q empty'. A listed position within a few pixels of a slot (e.g. [98, 153] for [99, 155]) is AT that slot; a frame in which two listed positions match no slot (containers in mid-swing at intermediate positions, e.g. [73, 140] and [101, 139] where the slots are [71, 123] and [103, 159]) is an 'empty' frame for the two slots nobody occupies in it. Listed positions carry no identity: a container can only be followed through slots, never by matching positions in the last frame to positions in the first. Do not stop at the first 'all at slots' frame and do not stop before the last frame; the final shuffle can sit in the frames just before the closing frames. Then group consecutive 'empty' frames into runs; each run is one SHUFFLE, and the number of runs is the number of shuffles, however many there are (one, two, three or more) and whether or not the same pair of slots repeats. Write out the list of shuffles in order (e.g. 'shuffle 1: slots P and Q, frames 80-96; shuffle 2: slots P and Q, frames 128-144; shuffle 3: slots Q and R, frames 176-192'). Then keep an explicit slot table (which container is at which slot, starting from the first container frame) and apply the shuffles one by one in time order, each time swapping the two containers whose slots were empty in that run, writing the table after every swap. Only after the last shuffle is applied read off the named container's slot. Parity cross-check, not a substitute: for the named container's pair, an even number of shuffles of that pair returns it to where it was before those shuffles, an odd number leaves it swapped; if the table and the parity disagree, recount the runs. Shuffles of pairs the named container is not in do not change its slot. The entry may only be written AFTER these four things have actually been written out in the answer: the frame-by-frame labels, the numbered list of shuffles, the slot table after each swap, and the parity check; a block of one or more consecutive 'empty' frames is one shuffle even when it is the only shuffle in the video. Whenever a shuffle empties the named container's own slot, the named container ends at the OTHER slot of that pair; so if its slot was emptied an odd number of times the entry must differ from the container that first sat over the cube. Every demonstration of this task contains at least one shuffle: an answer that finds zero shuffles, or that returns every named cube to its first container, has mislabelled frames and must be recounted; (4) never assume a container returns to its own starting slot, and never take the container resting nearest the cube's original position in the last frame; the entry is the named container's slot after every swap, written with that slot's coordinates as listed in the last demonstration frame. Worked example (two cubes, two different pairs each shuffle once, so BOTH named containers move): green cube at [92, 156], blue cube at [125, 117]; first container frame lists [80, 121], [89, 157], [123, 116], [131, 154]; green's slot is [89, 157], blue's is [123, 116]; frames 80-96 list two positions matching no slot while [123, 116] and [131, 154] stay, so 'slots [80, 121] and [89, 157] empty'; frame 112 'all at slots'; frames 128-160 'slots [123, 116] and [131, 154] empty'; last frame 'all at slots'. Shuffle 1 swaps [80, 121] and [89, 157]: green now at [80, 121]. Shuffle 2 swaps [123, 116] and [131, 154]: blue now at [131, 154]. Last frame lists those slots as [82, 121] and [131, 154]; entry [[82, 121], [131, 154]]. Second worked example (three shuffles, the last two of the same pair, the last one just before the closing frames): goal names green then red; green cube at [82, 128], red cube at [127, 146]; containers first rest at [80, 129], [96, 88], [128, 145], [110, 172]; green's container is at slot [80, 129], red's at slot [128, 145]; labelling every frame to the end: frames 64-80 'slots [96, 88] and [110, 172] empty', frame 96 'all at slots', frames 112-128 'slots [80, 129] and [128, 145] empty', frame 144 'all at slots', frames 160-176 'slots [80, 129] and [128, 145] empty', frames 192-208 'all at slots' (last frame). Shuffle 1 swaps [96, 88] and [110, 172]: green still at [80, 129], red still at [128, 145]. Shuffle 2 swaps [80, 129] and [128, 145]: green at [128, 145], red at [80, 129]. Shuffle 3 swaps the same two: green back at [80, 129], red back at [128, 145]. Parity: two shuffles of green's pair, even, so green is where it started; agrees. Last frame lists those slots as [81, 129] and [129, 145]; entry [[81, 129], [129, 145]]. e.g. [[84, 110], [93, 163]]
fields.annotation: Ordered list of container positions [y, x], one per cube named in the goal instruction, in the order the goal names them; each entry is the position, at the last demonstration frame, of the container that ends up hiding that cube. Filled once at the first decision step from the demonstration, by slots and swaps: (1) in the first cube frames note each named cube's position; (2) at the first container frame, the named cube's container is the one resting nearest that cube; every container's resting position in that frame is its slot; (3) scan the frames after the first container frame in order and split them into runs: a run is a maximal block of consecutive frames in which two containers are away from their slots (off by well over 10 pixels, however their positions change inside the block), and it ends at the first following frame in which every container is again at a slot. Each run is exactly one shuffle, and it swaps the slots of the two containers whose slots are empty during that run. A later run, even of the same two slots, is a separate shuffle. List the runs in order, apply the swaps in order (an odd number of runs of a pair leaves them swapped, an even number leaves them where they started; runs of other pairs do not touch the named container), and only then read off the named container's slot; (4) the entry is the named cube's container's slot after all swaps, written with the coordinates listed for that slot in the last demonstration frame (slots wobble by a few pixels). Never changes afterwards; copied unchanged at every later step. e.g. [[84, 110], [93, 163]]

field target_containers, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  Ordered list of container positions [y, x], one per cube named in the goal instruction, in the order the goal names them; each entry is the position, at the last demonstration frame, of the container that ends up hiding that cube. Filled once at the first decision step and copied unchanged afterwards. Situation that mattered: at the first decision step, with an empty memory and the demonstration shown, the goal named a cube whose container took part in a shuffle; in every demonstration of this task a shuffle is a block of three consecutive frames in which exactly two containers leave their resting slots, circle each other, and come back to rest, and when they come back each of the two sits in the OTHER one's slot. The policy instead took the container resting at the named cube's original slot in the last frame, so it wrote the neighbour's position and pointed at the wrong container (PREDICTABILITY: the value written differed from the annotated one; SUFFICIENCY: the first pick then pointed at the wrong container). field target_containers, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  Same field, same meaning: ordered list of container positions [y, x], one per cube named in the goal, each the last-demonstration-frame position of the container that ends up hiding that cube. The filling procedure has to make shuffle-counting explicit, because a demonstration can contain two separate shuffles of the same pair of containers, separated by one or more frames in which every container is back at a slot; the policy treated all off-slot frames as a single shuffle and so recorded the container's position after the first swap only, pointing at the wrong container at the first decision step. This breaks PREDICTABILITY (the written value differs from the value the procedure yields). Replace step (3) with: scan the frames after the first container frame and split them into runs; a run is a maximal block of consecutive frames in which two containers are away from their slots (off by well over 10 pixels, however their positions change inside the block); a run ends at the first following frame in which every container is at a slot. Each run is exactly one shuffle, and it swaps the slots of the two containers whose slots are empty during that run. List the runs in order, apply the swaps in order, and only then read off the named container's slot. Two runs of the same pair cancel (odd number of runs of a pair = swapped, even = back where they started). Then step (4) as before: the entry is the named container's slot after all swaps, written with that slot's coordinates in the last demonstration frame. Never changes afterwards. e.g. [[101, 139]]

  Same field, same meaning and format. Rewrite step (3) so the policy counts shuffles one by one instead of treating every off-slot frame as part of one shuffle: after the first container frame, walk the frames in order and keep a running slot assignment. Two shuffles of the same pair put them back where they started; three put them swapped again. Rules at any decision step: (1) If the scene shows the gripper raised with fingers partly closed (about 46% open), it is holding a container: choose B (put down the container). (2) If the fingers are fully open (about 100%) and put_down_count is less than the number of entries in target_containers, choose A and point at the container whose current listed position is nearest to target_containers[put_down_count + 1] (1-based: the first entry when put_down_count is 0, the second when it is 1); write the point as that container's listed position. (3) If the fingers are fully open and put_down_count equals the number of entries, every named container has been handled; choose A and point at the last entry of target_containers again (harmless repeat). If a situation matches none of these rules (e.g. gripper state unclear), pick the rule whose gripper description is closest: partly closed fingers mean B, open fingers mean A on the next unhandled target.

fields.name: target_containers
fields.description: Ordered list of container positions [y, x], one per cube named in the goal instruction, in the order the goal names them. Write it at the first decision step (memory empty, demonstration steps shown) by this procedure, then copy it unchanged at every later step. Procedure: (1) from the first demonstration frames note each named cube's position; (2) at the first frame listing containers, the named cube's container is the one nearest that cube; the positions listed in that frame are the slots; label the named container by its slot; (3) go through EVERY container frame after the first one, in order, up to and including the last demonstration frame, and label each frame before doing anything else: either 'all at slots' or 'slots P and Q empty' (a container is off its slot when it is well over 10 pixels away). Do not stop at the first 'all at slots' frame and do not stop before the last frame; the final shuffle can sit in the frames just before the closing frames. Then group consecutive 'empty' frames into runs; each run is one SHUFFLE, and the number of runs is the number of shuffles, however many there are (one, two, three or more) and whether or not the same pair of slots repeats. Write out the list of shuffles in order (e.g. 'shuffle 1: slots P and Q, frames 80-96; shuffle 2: slots P and Q, frames 128-144; shuffle 3: slots Q and R, frames 176-192'). Then keep an explicit slot table (which container is at which slot, starting from the first container frame) and apply the shuffles one by one in time order, each time swapping the two containers whose slots were empty in that run, writing the table after every swap. Only after the last shuffle is applied read off the named container's slot. Parity cross-check, not a substitute: for the named container's pair, an even number of shuffles of that pair returns it to where it was before those shuffles, an odd number leaves it swapped; if the table and the parity disagree, recount the runs. Shuffles of pairs the named container is not in do not change its slot; (4) never assume a container returns to its own starting slot, and never take the container resting nearest the cube's original position in the last frame; the entry is the named container's slot after every swap, written with that slot's coordinates as listed in the last demonstration frame. Worked example: cube at [70, 119]; containers first rest at [66, 120], [84, 109], [93, 163], [119, 145]; the cube's container is [66, 120]; later frames show [66, 120] and [84, 109] both off their slots for three frames, then all back; those two swapped, so the cube's container is now the one at [84, 110] in the last frame; entry [84, 110]. Second worked example (three shuffles, the last two of the same pair, the last one just before the closing frames): goal names green then red; green cube at [82, 128], red cube at [127, 146]; containers first rest at [80, 129], [96, 88], [128, 145], [110, 172]; green's container is at slot [80, 129], red's at slot [128, 145]; labelling every frame to the end: frames 64-80 'slots [96, 88] and [110, 172] empty', frame 96 'all at slots', frames 112-128 'slots [80, 129] and [128, 145] empty', frame 144 'all at slots', frames 160-176 'slots [80, 129] and [128, 145] empty', frames 192-208 'all at slots' (last frame). Shuffle 1 swaps [96, 88] and [110, 172]: green still at [80, 129], red still at [128, 145]. Shuffle 2 swaps [80, 129] and [128, 145]: green at [128, 145], red at [80, 129]. Shuffle 3 swaps the same two: green back at [80, 129], red back at [128, 145]. Parity: two shuffles of green's pair, even, so green is where it started; agrees. Last frame lists those slots as [81, 129] and [129, 145]; entry [[81, 129], [129, 145]]. e.g. [[84, 110], [93, 163]]
fields.annotation: Ordered list of container positions [y, x], one per cube named in the goal instruction, in the order the goal names them; each entry is the position, at the last demonstration frame, of the container that ends up hiding that cube. Filled once at the first decision step from the demonstration, by slots and swaps: (1) in the first cube frames note each named cube's position; (2) at the first container frame, the named cube's container is the one resting nearest that cube; every container's resting position in that frame is its slot; (3) scan the frames after the first container frame in order and split them into runs: a run is a maximal block of consecutive frames in which two containers are away from their slots (off by well over 10 pixels, however their positions change inside the block), and it ends at the first following frame in which every container is again at a slot. Each run is exactly one shuffle, and it swaps the slots of the two containers whose slots are empty during that run. A later run, even of the same two slots, is a separate shuffle. List the runs in order, apply the swaps in order (an odd number of runs of a pair leaves them swapped, an even number leaves them where they started; runs of other pairs do not touch the named container), and only then read off the named container's slot; (4) the entry is the named cube's container's slot after all swaps, written with the coordinates listed for that slot in the last demonstration frame (slots wobble by a few pixels). Never changes afterwards; copied unchanged at every later step. e.g. [[84, 110], [93, 163]]

fields.name: put_down_count
fields.description: Number of containers picked up and then put down so far. Write 0 at the first decision step. Add one to the carried-in value when the execution steps of the current step show the fingers reopening from about 46% to about 100% after being lowered over a container (a put-down just completed); otherwise copy the carried-in value. e.g. 1
fields.annotation: Number of containers the robot has picked up and then put down so far in this episode. 0 at the first decision step; increases by one at the decision step whose execution steps show the fingers reopening (from about 46% back to about 100%) while over a container, i.e. the step right after a 'put down the container' subgoal finished. e.g. 1
